Subject: Baseline token profile + ask for committed run-rate sizing

Hi Olga / Kim,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. As promised I'm attaching the token profile for our current traffic (sample week) and a rough list of peak windows. Two quick asks so we can move the procurement conversation forward: 

1) Can Redwood give a recommended Dedicated slab (GPU count / slab type) that meets a 95th-pct latency SLO of <=400ms for our mix (document attached)?
2) For commercial sizing: what headroom multiplier would you bake in for quarterly peaking (we see 2.2x historical spikes) and cold-start warmups?

Attached: sierra_token_profile.csv and the expected P95 target doc. Procurement is requesting a ballpark by EOD Monday to start the internal CAPEX review.

Appreciate it —
Daniel
Director, Platform Engineering
Sierra Systems

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@sierra-sys.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 13:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Baseline token profile + ask for committed run-rate sizing

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the profile. Quick summary after an initial pass:

- Traffic mix: ~65% short prompts (~30 tokens), 25% medium (~180 tokens), 10% long (>800 tokens).
- Peak cadence: daily spikes around 12:00-13:00 PT and a larger weekly spike on Tue mornings (2.0–2.4x).

Sizing recommendation (ballpark) to meet P95 <=400ms:
- Model baseline: Llama2-70B-quant (production-equivalent) and a smaller fallback Mistral-7b-quant for very high-concurrency events.
- Tokens/sec target: steady-state 18k tokens/sec sustained, peak observed bursts ~45k tokens/sec; plan for committed slab capable of 40k sustained TPS with burst to 70k using burst capacity and routing policies.
- GPU slab: 6x H100-80GB cabinets (or equivalent A100 v4 8-GPU pods depending on region) for the primary slab. With our runtime optimizations (KV caching on short prompts) this maps to the 40k sustained TPS number with P95 ~360–380ms in our projection.

Headroom guidance:
- Operational headroom: 1.8x nominal (sufficient for routine daily spikes).
- Commercial peaking buffer to propose in contract: 2.5x for first 90 days while patterns stabilize, re-evaluate at Q1 review.

Caveats and assumptions:
- Estimates assume prefix/KV cache hit rates of 45% on short prompt traffic. If cache hits drop below 25% we recommend +2 GPUs to maintain P95.
- Token/sec mapping depends on average output length; long-response tails can push P95 above target if tail probability increases.

Next steps: I'll run a scenario table with explicit GPU counts (H100 vs A100 tradeoffs), latency sensitivity if cache hit varies, and an ops fallback (auto-route to smaller model at >80% slab utilization). Can you confirm procurement needs a formal slide deck or raw numbers table?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: sierra_tf_estimates.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, Daniel Park <daniel.park@sierra-sys.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Baseline token profile + ask for committed run-rate sizing

Thanks — adding the price/run-rate framing and SLA implications. A few specifics to pair with Olga's ops numbers: 

- Commitment tiers we recommend for Sierra: 1) Starter: 6-month reserved (40k nominal TPS) with 2.0x burst credit bank, 2) Growth: 12-month reserved (60k nominal TPS) with 2.5x burst.
- SLA: we can offer P95 latency objective mapping to the slab configuration with a credit schedule if p95 breaches are attributable to capacity shortages (we exclude customer-side rate spikes beyond agreed traffic profile).
- Pricing delta: H100 hardware premium ~18% vs A100-based pods; for Sierra's region our margin-optimized recommendation is A100 v4 pods unless the customer wants single-architecture (H100) for reduced variance.

Operational fallback plan to include in proposal:
- Canary route with Mistral-7b-quant (lower cost per token) automatically used when utilization >85% and latency threatens SLO.
- Auto-scaling policy to add 2x burst nodes for predictable weekly peaks (pre-warmed if scheduled).

I'll draft the financial slide. Olga — please include the worst-case p95 if cache hit = 15% so procurement can see downside.

Kim
Head of Solutions Pricing | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf (pdf)]
